name: Intel Gaudi 3
disclaimer: Die, DCORE, MME and HBM footprints are illustrative and drawn to a common scale (1 unit = 4 mm); exact die dimensions are not publicly disclosed. DCORE/MME/TPC floorplans follow the white paper's block diagrams but are not literal layouts.

components.name: OAM package substrate
components.desc: Open Compute Project OAM 2.0 mezzanine card. Carries power and signals from the two compute dies to the host system; rated up to 900W TDP.

specs.label: Form factor
specs.value: OCP OAM 2.0 mezzanine (also offered as a PCIe Gen5 x16 add-in card, 600W)

components.name: Interposer bridge
components.desc: Package-level interposer joining the two compute dies and the surrounding HBM2e stacks. The die-to-die link it carries is transparent to software: both dies present as one logical accelerator.

specs.label: Packaging
specs.value: Two dies + 8 HBM2e stacks on a shared substrate (specific interposer technology not named in the white paper)

components.name: Compute die 0
components.desc: One of two identical compute dies. Each die holds 2 DCOREs (4 MMEs, 32 TPCs), half the on-die SRAM, HBM PHYs, and a share of the media and network engines.

specs.label: Die-to-die interconnect
specs.value: High-bandwidth, low-latency link over the interposer; behaves as one unified die to software

components.name: Compute die 1
components.desc: Second compute die, identical to die 0.

components.name: Die-to-die bridge
components.desc: The interposer link between die 0 and die 1. Intel describes it only as high-bandwidth and low-latency, with no public bandwidth figure; it makes the two dies behave as one accelerator at the software level.

specs.label: Latency/bandwidth
specs.value: Not publicly disclosed (described as high-bandwidth, low-latency)

components.name: HBM2e base die (die 0 side)
components.desc: Logic/PHY base die at the bottom of each HBM2e stack feeding die 0.

components.name: HBM2e DRAM layers (die 0 side)
components.desc: 4 of the 8 HBM2e stacks, stacked DRAM over TSVs, running at 3.6 GHz. Weights and KV cache live here; decoding is HBM-bandwidth bound.

specs.label: Capacity (chip total)
specs.value: 128 GB across 8 HBM2e stacks (16 GB each)

components.name: HBM2e base die (die 1 side)
components.desc: Logic/PHY base die at the bottom of each HBM2e stack feeding die 1.

components.name: HBM2e DRAM layers (die 1 side)
components.desc: The other 4 of the 8 HBM2e stacks, feeding die 1.

components.name: HBM PHY / memory controller (die 0)
components.desc: Memory controller and HBM2e PHY turning L3/L2 misses into reads/writes against die 0's 4 HBM2e stacks.

components.name: HBM PHY / memory controller (die 1)
components.desc: Memory controller and HBM2e PHY for die 1's 4 HBM2e stacks.

components.name: DCORE 0 L2 cache (24 MB)
components.desc: One of four 24 MB L2 slices carved from the chip's 96 MB on-die SRAM. The SRAM can instead be used as a single flat, uniformly-accessible L3 cache; the Gaudi software stack chooses per-tensor.

components.name: MME (DCORE 0, engine 0)
components.desc: One of the chip's 8 Matrix Multiplication Engines. Each MME is a large 256x256, 64K-MAC systolic array dedicated to GEMMs: fully-connected layers, convolutions, batched matmuls. Click Open to see inside.

components.name: MME (DCORE 0, engine 1)
components.desc: Second MME of DCORE 0.

components.name: TPCs (DCORE 0, x16)
components.desc: 16 Tensor Processor Cores of DCORE 0 — VLIW SIMD engines handling every non-GEMM op (elementwise, activations, normalization, softmax) between MME passes.

components.name: DCORE 1 L2 cache (24 MB)
components.desc: Second 24 MB L2 slice on die 0, local to DCORE 1.

components.name: MME (DCORE 1, engine 0)
components.desc: First MME of DCORE 1.

components.name: MME (DCORE 1, engine 1)
components.desc: Second MME of DCORE 1.

components.name: TPCs (DCORE 1, x16)
components.desc: 16 Tensor Processor Cores of DCORE 1.

components.name: DCORE 2 L2 cache (24 MB)
components.desc: Third 24 MB L2 slice, local to DCORE 2 on die 1.

components.name: MME (DCORE 2, engine 0)
components.desc: First MME of DCORE 2.

components.name: MME (DCORE 2, engine 1)
components.desc: Second MME of DCORE 2.

components.name: TPCs (DCORE 2, x16)
components.desc: 16 Tensor Processor Cores of DCORE 2.

components.name: DCORE 3 L2 cache (24 MB)
components.desc: Fourth 24 MB L2 slice, local to DCORE 3 on die 1. Together the 4 slices make up the chip's 96 MB on-die SRAM.

components.name: MME (DCORE 3, engine 0)
components.desc: First MME of DCORE 3.

components.name: MME (DCORE 3, engine 1)
components.desc: Second MME of DCORE 3.

components.name: TPCs (DCORE 3, x16)
components.desc: 16 Tensor Processor Cores of DCORE 3.

components.name: Media engine (14 DEC + 4 ROT)
components.desc: Fixed-function media subsystem shared by both dies: 14 video/image decoder engines (HEVC, H.264, VP9, JPEG up to 8192x8192) and 4 rotator engines (2D/3D rotation, projection, mesh distort, re-sample).

components.name: PCIe Gen5 x16 host link
components.desc: Host interface: PCIe Gen5 x16, carrying the Graph Compiler's binaries and host-managed I/O.

components.name: 24x 200 GbE RoCE ports
components.desc: 24 integrated 200 Gbps RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet) NIC ports plus 4 RDMA aggregation engines, all on-die. Unlike designs that pair NVLink for scale-up with separate host NICs for scale-out, Gaudi 3 uses the same Ethernet ports and RDMA engines for both: card-to-card inside a node and switch-to-switch across racks.

specs.label: Ports
specs.value: 24 x 200 Gbps (48 x 112G PAM4 SerDes lanes)

specs.label: Aggregate bandwidth
specs.value: 1,200 GB/s bidirectional, RoCE Ethernet (not NVLink) — same fabric for scale-up and scale-out

specs.label: RDMA aggregation engines
specs.value: 4, perform collective (e.g. all-reduce) summation on behalf of the communication library

components.name: MME systolic array (256x256)
components.desc: The MME's 256x256 grid of Multiply-Accumulate units (64K MACs total). Weight-stationary matmul: operands stream in from cache/HBM, each PE multiplies and forwards partial sums across the array. One large MME instead of many small cores needs far less input bandwidth per MAC — roughly 16x less than an equivalent grid of small cores.

specs.label: Supported input datatypes
specs.value: FP8 (E4M3, E5M2), BF16, FP16, TF32, FP32

specs.label: On-the-fly FP8 scaling
specs.value: Yes — reduces TPC load when converting to/from FP8

components.name: FP32 accumulator
components.desc: All MME datatypes accumulate into FP32, no matter the input precision. Partial sums build up here across the K dimension before the result tile is written back.

components.name: TPC vector processing unit
components.desc: 256-byte-wide VLIW SIMD vector unit — the heart of the Tensor Processor Core. Runs every non-GEMM op: elementwise math, activations, normalization, softmax, reductions, with built-in deep-learning instructions.

components.name: TPC scalar unit
components.desc: Handles control flow and address generation alongside the vector unit.

components.name: Tensor register file
components.desc: Register file feeding the vector processing unit.

components.name: TPC L1 cache
components.desc: Local cache backing the TPC's DMA-free programming model: unlike a typical DSP, the TPC reads and writes operands straight from cache or HBM without software managing a DMA engine.

components.name: Load/store unit
components.desc: Issues loads/stores directly against cache or HBM; lets kernels run back-to-back with no idle time between them, even for very small, microsecond-scale kernels.

steps.text: 1. Two Gaudi 3 compute dies (TSMC 5nm) sit on a shared substrate, joined by an interposer bridge — software sees one accelerator.
2. Weights and activations live across 8 HBM2e stacks — 128 GB total at 3.7 TB/s aggregate bandwidth.
3. A memory controller (HBM2e PHY) on each die reads the 4 HBM2e stacks attached to it.
4. If the data lives in the other die's HBM, it crosses the interposer bridge — invisible to software.
5. Data lands in the 96 MB on-die SRAM — used here as a 24 MB L2 slice per DCORE, or as one flat L3 cache.
6. Each DCORE's 2 MMEs pull A/B tiles into their 256x256, 64K-MAC systolic arrays and multiply.
7. Partial sums accumulate in FP32 inside the MME, regardless of input precision (FP8/BF16/FP16/TF32/FP32).
8. In parallel, the DCORE's 16 TPCs — 256B-wide VLIW SIMD cores — run non-GEMM ops (activation, normalization) straight from cache, with no DMA to manage.
9. Results write back through the on-die SRAM to HBM2e.
10. For multi-card training, the 24x200 GbE RoCE ports and RDMA aggregation engines run collective all-reduce directly over Ethernet — card-to-card inside the node (scale-up).
11. The same 24 ports also carry traffic across racks (scale-out) — one fabric for both, unlike designs that split a proprietary scale-up link from a separate scale-out NIC.

summary.value: 2 identical dies, bridged via an on-package interposer (software-transparent)
900 W TDP (HL-325L OAM; PCIe card HL-338 is 600 W)
96 MB on-die SRAM (4 x 24 MB, configurable as L2 or a unified L3)
1,200 GB/s bidirectional — 24x200 GbE RoCE Ethernet, not NVLink; the same ports serve scale-up and scale-out
128 GB/s PCIe Gen5 x16 host link (64 GB/s per direction)
Two compute dies + 8 HBM2e stacks on a shared OAM substrate (interposer bridge; specific packaging tech not named)

scale.basis: Illustrative only — Intel has not published Gaudi 3 die dimensions. Package modeled on the OAM mezzanine form factor shown in the white paper.
